cues: A bright brass fanfare announces a dignitary's entrance, lending the procession a sense of ceremony.
In jazz, a soloist bends a sustained note into a bluesy cry above the rhythm section.
Clear high-register phrases let the lead part rise above a full orchestral texture.
A sharp, ringing call can signal a parade's turn before the marching band reaches the corner.
Muted, softened phrases create an intimate color in a late-night jazz arrangement.
Punchy offbeat riffs give a swing arrangement crisp accents between the singer's phrases.
